summary.headline: Borosil H1 FY27 revenue rose 8.8% to INR 627.4 crore and gross margin expanded 390 bps to 65.2%, helped by price hikes, mix and solar savings.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 8.8% YoY to INR 627.4 crore, with gross profit up 15.6% to INR 408.9 crore and EBITDA (excluding other income) up 20.5% to INR 107.7 crore. PAT improved to INR 44.7 crore from INR 40.1 crore. Management credited calibrated price increases of roughly 2.5-7% across categories, better mix, operational efficiencies and captive solar savings, partly offset by West Asia-linked input cost inflation. Glassware growth was muted (2.7%) because the Diwali shift moved B2B demand, while non-glassware grew 10.9% and Opalware 7.8%. DGTR issued final findings on 24 September 2026 recommending five-year anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate glassware, pending Ministry of Finance notification.

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 sales INR 210.7 crore vs INR 195.4 crore, up 7.8%. Management said growth reflected 3-7% price increases plus premiumisation and some volume growth.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavable, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR 152.6 crore vs INR 148.6 crore, up 2.7%. Management attributed the softness to the Diwali calendar shift moving B2B demand.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, insulated bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 turnover INR 240.2 crore vs INR 216.6 crore, up 10.9%. Management said Q2 growth was broad-based and not mainly restocking; Hydra sales rose over 30% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Management said the current growth momentum and EBITDA margins should be sustainable, but gave no numeric guidance for H2 revenue, margin or capex.
Long-term target of 15-20% revenue CAGR reiterated; management declined to extrapolate Q2+Q3 growth.
Solar phase 3 gives about INR 30 crore annual EBITDA savings; phase 4 adds about INR 12 crore per annum from Q4 FY27 (INR 16-17 crore of phase 1-2 savings already in FY26).

Anti-dumping duty: Ministry of Finance notification due within about 90 days of 24 September 2026, i.e. by about 24 December 2026. Management said the duty would mainly reduce inventory, not lift prices or margins.
Vision 2030 plan to be announced by end of FY27, with capex to be shared over the next one to two quarters after approval.
Further price hikes depend on evolution of gas and LPG costs; last price increase was taken at end of Q1/start of Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Two double-wall Hydra lines in Rajasthan (Stylenest India) commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line delayed from December 2026 to January 2027 due to port congestion. Both lines already above 80% utilisation.

Captive solar at Bikaner: 35.8 MWp commissioned in three phases with 16.9 MWh BESS; solar now meets about 60% of power requirements. Additional 6.5 MWp with 5.0 MWh BESS (INR 27.6 crore) under implementation; 3.0 MWp for Hydra (INR 10.0 crore) expected in Q4 FY27.
Borosilicate Pressware furnace expansion at Jaipur from 25 TPD to 32 TPD with a third forming line, capex INR 50 crore, commissioning by end of Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation is 90%.
New glassware facility at Bharuch will be set up and funded by Borosil Scientific Ltd instead of Borosil, subject to approvals.
Solar phase 4 capex of about INR 37 crore to follow.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 2.5-3% in Opalware in some ranges, 3-5% in some ranges and 5-7% in others, effective from Q2 FY27.
Management said October 2026 showed good momentum across categories and channels, with trade and B2B strong, followed by e-commerce and LFS, and new premium products well received.

Working capital rose about 20-25 days YoY at September, which management attributed mainly to Diwali timing and inventory built up from dumped imports and BIS challenges. Management said the inventory should be read on a March-to-March basis.
Management said non-glassware growth was not mainly restocking; channel inventory was built partly from low vacuum-bottle capacity earlier.
Management said Borosil competes on quality and differentiation rather than price, citing a 25%+ CAGR in the appliances category.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest execution risk in moving toward appliances, and how will margins and share be protected against price undercutting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appliances are not growing at the cost of glassware, that glass is still a market-adoption category, and that Borosil competes on quality, not price.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk to margins once the Diwali-related lift fades, and which external cost pressures matter most?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG and raw-material pressure eased from Q1 to Q2, price pass-through improved and solar phase 3 savings will support sustained margins, but future gas-cost increases remain undecided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the solar savings is in the numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 3 gives about INR 30 crore annual EBITDA savings (incremental INR 13 crore over FY26), with a further INR 12 crore from phase 4 from Q4 FY27. Q2 expenses were about 5.3% of sales vs 7.2% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR 1.2 crore government grant in cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a capital subsidy on Opalware and borosilicate furnace expansions, not revenue. Total incentive is about INR 55 crore, with the balance to be received in future years and deducted from fixed assets.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the YoY gross margin rise and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price increases, efficiency and cost actions, and Hydra double-wall lines. It declined to quantify the split beyond the Opalware 2.5-3% price increase.

qa_highlights.question: When will the anti-dumping duty take effect and what is the financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The Ministry of Finance has about 90 days from 24 September 2026, so by about 24 December. Management said there is no direct margin or pricing benefit; the main effect is lower inventory and better growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the stainless-steel third double-wall line and when will its margin benefit show?
qa_highlights.answer: The third line slipped about a month to January 2027 due to port congestion, with some impact expected from end Q4 FY27 after stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for inventory reduction and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not give a number; sales are being drawn from year-1 and year-2 inventory built for a larger market, and focus is on volume growth to bring inventory down.

risks_watch: Anti-dumping duty notification by Ministry of Finance is due around 24 December 2026. Management said there will be no direct margin or pricing benefit, so the gain depends on volume recovery.
Gas and LPG cost volatility from the West Asia conflict; further price hikes are undecided and depend on how the situation evolves.
Q2 margin pattern is seasonally lower; management said like-to-like margin comparison should wait until end Q3.
Working capital and inventory remain elevated (about 20-25 days higher YoY at September); no reduction target given.
Glassware growth is soft (2.7%), while Hydra's third double-wall line is delayed to January 2027.
Net debt of INR 95.8 crore with rising depreciation and finance costs (INR 51.8 crore in H1).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand momentum and margin sustainability, but guarded on forward numbers: management gave no quantified H2 guidance and repeatedly deferred to future price and gas-cost developments. Some answers on Q2 gross margin seasonality and the glassware-versus-appliances trade-off were evasive or repetitive.

We are not in any category at the cost of any other category.
So, capacity utilization is not a challenge at all as far as hydra.

growth.why: Management reiterated a 15-20% long-term revenue CAGR without numeric H2 guidance; growth is partly backed by price hikes of 2.5-7%, Hydra line capacity already above 80% utilised, and a Jaipur furnace expansion (25 to 32 TPD, INR 50 crore) at 90% current utilisation, though that expansion is not live until end-FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose 390 bps to 65.2% and Q2 expenses fell to about 5.3% of sales vs 7.2%, with solar phase 3 (about INR 30 crore annual savings) and phase 4 (about INR 12 crore more from Q4 FY27) adding support, though management declined to quantify the split and gas costs remain a risk.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two Hydra double-wall lines are already live from 30 June 2026 and running above 80% utilisation, the third line is delayed to January 2027, and the 6.5 MWp and 3.0 MWp solar additions are under construction with Q4 FY27 expected; Jaipur furnace expansion (25 to 32 TPD) is not live until end Q4 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated a 15-20% long-term revenue CAGR and said October showed good momentum, but H1 revenue grew only 8.8% and glassware grew 2.7%, and no numeric H2 guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Furnace utilisation is 90% and Hydra lines are above 80%, with Vision 2030 plan due by end FY27 and capex to be shared over the next one to two quarters after approval; Jaipur expansion (INR 50 crore) is already approved.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said current momentum and EBITDA margins should be sustainable, but gave no numeric guidance and declined to extrapolate Q2 and Q3 growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas and LPG cost volatility from the West Asia conflict is unresolved, glassware growth is only 2.7%, and the Hydra third line slipped to January 2027, though H1 PAT still rose to INR 44.7 crore from INR 40.1 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said new premium products were well received in October 2026 and Hydra sales rose over 30% in Q2, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate glassware
rows.why: DGTR recommended five-year duty on 24 Sept 2026 and Ministry of Finance notification is due within about 90 days, but management said it mainly reduces inventory with no direct margin or price benefit.

rows.label: Inventory and working capital reduction
rows.why: Working capital is 20-25 days higher YoY at September and no reduction target was given; management says volume growth is the route to lower inventory, with March-to-March as the reference.

rows.label: Solar phase 4 savings from Q4 FY27
rows.why: Phase 4 adds about INR 12 crore a year on top of phase 3, taking total solar savings to about INR 42 crore annually, with about INR 37 crore capex to follow.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand momentum, price pass-through and solar savings, but cautious on forward numbers, giving no quantified H2 guidance and deferring to gas-cost and duty developments; analysts pushed on Q2 margin seasonality, the glassware versus appliances trade-off and inventory.
